headline: The low-observable Naval Strike Missile (NSM) carries a 120 kg penetrating warhead and has a range of 200–300 km, depending on the variant, with a top speed of approximately 1,100 km/h. During the cruise phase, it is guided by GPS/INS in combination with Terrain Contour Matching (TERCOM), which compares the terrain below with a preloaded digital map. In the terminal phase, a passive imaging infrared (IIR) seeker with automatic target recognition (ATR) takes over to engage the target. Plans to supply these missile systems to Ukraine had been discussed since 2023, but until now there had been been no official confirmation that they had been delivered.

headline: France pushed for strict EU defence-fund rules that limited participation by non-EU companies, including those with UK links. Those same rules have now backfired. Paris received €15.1bn instead of the €16.2bn it requested from the EU's €150bn SAFE fund, after some Franco-British projects, particularly involving missile maker MBDA, were deemed ineligible. The rules require 65% of funded defence products to originate within the EU, plus Norway, Iceland, or Ukraine. Since the UK has not finalized an agreement to contribute financially to the scheme, many joint UK-EU defence projects cannot qualify. Source: FT
